learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to solve problems effectively
Develop the ability to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire autonomous learning ability and concern for knowledge and continuous training
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions

syllabus_topics: BASIC CONCEPTS OF ELASTICITY AND STRENGTH OF MATERIALS
Internal forces in a section. Stress diagrams
Types of stresses in a section
Stress distribution. Simple stresses (Tension or compression, Pure bending, Pure shear, Pure torsion)
Stress distribution. Combined stresses (Skew bending, Compound bending)
Introduction and objectives of the topic
Estimation of the approximate deformed shape
Differential equation of the elastic curve
Calculation of displacements and rotations using the differential equation of the elastic curve
Calculation of forces in isostatic structures (Node method, Section method)
Calculation of displacements by energy theorems (Castigliano's Theorem, Unit Load Method)
Stiffness matrix of a bar in local coordinates.
Stiffness matrix of a bar in global coordinates.
Calculation of forces at bar ends (Axial forces).
Special cases in matrix calculation (Temperature variations, Elastic supports)
teaching_methods: Assignments, reports, memoranda and evaluation tests
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is based on two tests (40% each) and practical activities (20%), with a minimum score of 5/10 required for each component. If any minimum is not met, the overall grade will be 'FAIL'. For the second sitting, students must retake only the failed components, maintaining the minimum score for each. Exceptional assessment also consists of two theoretical-practical tests (40% each) and practical activities (20%), all with a minimum score of 5/10.
